data.title: Riot Platforms, Flowserve gain after Starboard pitches at C4K Investors Conference
data.description:
Riot Platforms (RIOT) climbed 9.4%, and Flowserve (FLS) advanced 1.8% after Starboard Value pitched the ideas at the C4K Investors Conference. 

Starboard's Jeff Smith pitched the long ideas at the C4K Investors Conference in Toronto on Wednesday, according to a copy of the presentations given at the charity conference in Toronto.

Bloomberg reported in April that Starboard had built a significant stake in Flowserve (FLS) and was seeking potential changes. Starboard, in a May letter to the board, said Flowserve (FLS) must improve its margins or risk falling behind competitors.

Flowserve (FLS) can achieve high-single-digit or better revenue growth, especially with a record backlog entering its next fiscal year, Starboard said in its presentation on Wednesday. Flowserve could also achieve operating margins above 22% by 2030. 

The activist also believes disruptions in the Middle East that have delayed equipment deliveries can turn into tailwinds, the activist said at the conference. 

Starboard owned 3.4 million shares of Flowserve (FLS) as of Sept. 30, making it one of the top 10 largest holders. 

The activist argues that Riot Platforms (RIOT) can unlock more value by converting to a real estate investment trust or selling itself to an established data center REIT or infrastructure investor, according to the presentation on Wednesday.

Starboard owned 10.5 million shares of RIOT as of Sept. 30, making the firm the 5th biggest holder with a 2.8% stake. News of the Starboard pitches was earlier reported by Bloomberg.

data.title: Nissan focuses on lower costs as Chinese automakers gain ground in Mexico
data.description:
Nissan Motor (NSANY) is using its experience in Mexico to prepare for a potential challenge from Chinese automakers in the US, as the Japanese manufacturer seeks to lower production costs and rebuild its market position.

Christian Meunier, chairman of Nissan Americas, said the company is facing growing competition from Chinese brands in Mexico, where they have rapidly secured about 10% of the market. The country is serving as a testing ground for strategies that could help Nissan (NSANY) compete with lower-cost rivals if they eventually enter the US.

Meunier said Nissan (NSANY) has roughly two years to improve its cost structure before Chinese manufacturers begin producing vehicles in Mexico to avoid import tariffs. The company is pursuing shorter development cycles, simpler engineering, greater automation, and supply chain savings.

Nissan's (NSANY) immediate priority remains reviving its US business, where its market share has recovered to around 6% after declining significantly over the past decade.

The automaker is preparing a series of new models, beginning with a hybrid version of its Rogue SUV. It also plans to bring back the Xterra later in the decade as part of a broader expansion of rugged sport utility vehicles.

Although tariffs and restrictions on Chinese automotive software currently limit their US entry, Meunier believes Nissan (NSANY) must prepare for their possible arrival within five to 10 years.

data.title: U.S. aircraft carrier leaves Middle East after reinforcements arrive
data.description:
The USS George Washington carrier strike group departed the Persian Gulf region and may be returning to Yokosuka, Japan, Bloomberg News reported Wednesday, citing two U.S. officials who requested anonymity. It was one of three American carrier groups deployed to support the naval blockade against Iran.

For investors, the departure changes the military posture around a region critical to global energy supplies. It does not by itself establish that tensions are easing: the arrival of another carrier preserves US military options, leaving uncertainty over renewed fighting and potential disruption to shipping.

The USS Theodore Roosevelt strike group arrived Monday, expanding President Donald Trump’s options should he resume active hostilities against Iran. U.S. Central Command published an image Wednesday showing the Roosevelt and George Washington sailing together.

The George Washington reached the region in August, leaving the western Pacific without a U.S. aircraft carrier. Analysts had warned that China might seek to exploit that absence.

Before this year’s Iran operations, the United States last deployed three carrier strike groups to the Middle East during the opening phase of the Iraq invasion in 2003.

data.title: Eli Lilly gains CV reduction risk indication for Mounjaro in Canada
data.description:
• Health Canada has approved a new indication for Eli Lilly's (LLY) Mounjaro (tirzepatide) to lower the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events in individuals with type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease.
  • Approval was based on results from the SURPASS-CVOT trial, which found Mounjaro non-inferiority to Trulicity (dulaglutide), an older GLP-1 marketed by Lilly with an established cardiovascular benefit. Mounjaro had an 8% lower rate of cardiovascular death, heart attack, or stroke compared to Trulicity.
  • Mounjaro, a dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist, was already approved in Canada as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve blood sugar in adults and children 10 years of age and older.

data.title: SOLV Energy raised to Buy at UBS after strong backlog growth
data.description:
SOLV Energy (MWH) rose 0.9% in Wednesday's trading as UBS upgraded the power industry infrastructure services provider to Buy from Neutral with a $37 price target, saying the market is underappreciating some key tailwinds given the current uncertainty around data center demand and higher interest rates.

SOLV (MWH) shares peaked at ~$47, up 87% from the February 2026 IPO price of $25, but they have since dropped back to roughly the original IPO price despite two acquisitions, beating and raising guidance in Q2 and Q3 and raising backlog 37% Y/Y to $9.2B since the IPO, providing an attractive entry point for investors, UBS analyst Jon Windham said.

The analyst also noted M&A upside potential, with continued expansion into adjacent services broadening SOLV's (MWH) scope of work and supporting earnings growth, and that the U.S. midterm election likely provides a Senate firewall to protect support for clean energy, resulting in a renewed focus on non-polluting energy sources for data center development.

data.title: Pain in TQQQ, SOXL may offer silver lining for tech stocks - SocGen
data.description:
Investors in the largest U.S. triple-leveraged technology exchange-traded funds have nearly erased tens of billions of dollars in 2026 paper profits, even as the underlying unleveraged funds remain solidly positive for the year, according to data from Societe Generale Cross Asset Research.

Aggregate 2026 investor profit and loss on the ProShares UltraPro QQQ ETF (TQQQ) and the Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull 3X ETF (SOXL)—which offer 3x leveraged exposure to the Nasdaq-100 (QQQ) and semiconductors (SOXX), respectively—has fallen back to roughly breakeven in November.

At their mid-year peaks around late June and July, SocGen noted, cumulative investor gains had reached roughly $17B for TQQQ and almost $40B for SOXL before an autumn selloff wiped out the advances.

With daily leverage resetting compound losses during choppy swings, TQQQ and SOXL holders now sit near flat on the year while their unleveraged underlying ETFs remain up some 7.5% and 40% year-to-date.

Still, strategists noted that the washout could signal a contrarian silver lining for U.S. tech stocks (XLK). When aggregate capital invested in Korean leveraged single-stock ETFs (SKHL) tipped into losses at the end of July, that inflection point marked a local bottom for the underlying shares—a pattern SocGen thinks is now worth watching in U.S. technology.

data.title: Nike eyes cricket as a way to grow sales in India aggressively
data.description:
Nike (NKE) is shifting some of its global priorities to target the high-growth sports market in India. The athletic apparel company has a goal to triple its business in India in just five years.

The company is investing to build its portfolio of running, training, and sportswear products in the country. An area of emphasis will be cricket, where Nike (NKE) plans to expand offerings, support grassroots programs, and add partnerships. Nike (NKE) has already partnered with the billionaire Mukesh Ambani-owned Mumbai Indians team and set plans to open a new campus in India.

Of note, India's athletic footwear and apparel market is estimated at $9B and is projected to grow over 10% annually to roughly $14B by 2030–2031.

Shares of Nike (NKE) were up 1.5% in late Wednesday trading.

data.title: Leopold Aschenbrenner plots 'Situational Awareness 2.0' comeback - report
data.description:
Leopold Aschenbrenner is plotting an reboot for his hedge fund Situational Awareness just four months after the AI-focused vehicle nearly collapsed under leveraged bets and required an emergency rescue from billionaire Ken Griffin's Citadel, according to a media report published Wednesday.

In recent weeks, the 25-year-old has discussed plans for "Situational Awareness 2.0" with prime brokers and investors, including a return to leveraged trading and raising new capital, the Financial Times reported, citing people with knowledge of the matter.

The move represents a reversal from July, when Aschenbrenner issued a mea culpa vowing he would no longer borrow money from lenders to amplify his bets. His success hinges on convincing Wall Street he can manage risk after assets plunged from more than $20B to needing an emergency rescue in a matter of days this past summer. The fund still manages more than $10B, mainly in private stakes, the FT reported.

Situational Awareness holds an approximately $5B stake in AI giant Anthropic (ANT)—where Aschenbrenner's wife serves as chief of staff to CEO Dario Amodei—that is expected to appreciate markedly after the initial public offering.

Aschenbrenner has also discussed raising additional capital from outside investors in the new year, though plans have not been finalized, people involved in the talks said, the FT reported.

Aschenbrenner reportedly has been in discussions with Jefferies (JEF) to set up a prime brokerage account, following an earlier rejection this year over concerns that the fund wasn't adequately hedged. Meanwhile, Situational Awareness is also partnering with the specialist brokerage Clear Street.

The San Francisco-based hedge fund during the summer had to strike an emergency deal with Citadel to offload most of its public equities at a discount in order to repay lenders like Goldman Sachs (GS) and JPMorgan Chase (JPM)—both of which had provided financing despite Aschenbrenner's minimal trading background. JPMorgan later terminated its lending to the fund. Situational Awareness continues to oversee a modest public portfolio that includes positions in SharonAI (SHAZ) and data center developer CleanSpark (CLSK).

data.title: UniFirst/Cintas deal spread narrows on report companies optimistic for FTC approval
data.description:
The deal spread in Cintas's (CTAS) planned $5.5 billion purchase of UniFirst (UNF) narrowed after a report that the companies are cautiously optimistic that the Federal Trade Commission will clear the combination unconditionally and are planning for integration. The spread narrowed to $89 from $100 on Tuesday.

The FTC, which is still probing the deal, hasn't come to a decision, and the two companies are working on other methods for clearance, according to traders, who cited a Capitol Forum report that was circulating on Wednesday. UniFirst (UNF) executives met Tuesday to discuss ways to close the deal. 

The FTC staff has concerns that combining the two largest rental and cleaning uniforms companies could leave big customers without alternatives, according to the report. 

The latest report comes after Semafor on Friday reported that the FTC will soon have a “last rites” meeting with the parties. These meetings between the antitrust regulator and the parties are typically a precursor to a formal lawsuit. 

Sources told the Capitol Forum that several meetings have been scheduled this week between the companies and the FTC, but the talks are just part of the normal review. 

Semafor reported late last month that the FTC plans to sue to block a combination of uniform companies. The antitrust regulator had not voted on its decision, and it had not yet held a formal "last-rites" meeting.

Last month UniFirst (UNF) and Cintas (CTAS) disclosed that they certified with the FTC that each had substantially complied with the regulator's second request. Cintas and UniFirst entered into a timing agreement with the FTC pursuant to which they would not consummate the deal before Dec. 11.

Uniform retail firm Cintas (CTAS) agreed to acquire smaller rival UniFirst (UNF) for $310 per share in cash and stock in March, representing an enterprise value of about $5.5B.

data.title: Comstock Resources cut to Sell equivalent, CNX Resources raised at Morgan Stanley
data.description:
Comstock Resources (CRK) fell 2.4% in Wednesay's trading as Morgan Stanley downgraded the oil and gas company to Underweight from Equal Weight with a $13 price target, saying the shares currently trade ~20% above the bank's net asset value at strip pricing.

Comstock (CRK) announced in September a $1.65B strategic partnership with Azerbaijan's SOCAR in exchange for non-operating working interests in its legacy and Western Haynesville assets; concurrently, Comstock majority owner Jerry Jones entered into a joint venture to fund the drilling and completion costs of some legacy and Western Haynesville wells in exchange for an ownership stake.

Morgan Stanley analyst Devin McDermott said while he views the transactions positively, as they improve Comstock's (CRK) liquidity position, he still forecasts an outspend in 2027 at $3 Henry Hub.

The bank also upgraded CNX Resources (CNX) to Equal Weight from Underweight with a $36 PT, saying the company is the most hedged gas E&P within its coverage, with nearly 80% of 2027 production protected, supporting relatively stable cash flow even at lower Henry Hub prices.
